card.lives_in: Batley, West Yorkshire (Yorkshire and The Humber)
card.occupation: Upholsterer. She has been self-employed for nine years, working from a rented unit on a small industrial estate. She reupholsters armchairs, dining chairs, headboards and the odd vintage settee, and does some contract work for a pub chain and two care homes.
card.education_detail: Left secondary school in Dewsbury at 16 with GCSEs including a B in Art and a C in Maths. Did a two-year apprenticeship at a furniture manufacturer in Heckmondwike with an NVQ Level 2, later Level 3, in upholstery. Took an evening bookkeeping course at the local college when she went self-employed.
card.household: Lives with her husband Darren (50), a maintenance fitter at a food factory, in a three-bed semi they have owned for 19 years. Their son Lewis (23) moved to Leeds two years ago and comes back most Sundays for his tea. They have an elderly Border terrier called Mabel.
card.cultural_background: White British and West Yorkshire through and through. Her dad worked in a textile mill until it closed and her mum was a school dinner lady. She was brought up loosely C of E but hasn't been to church since her wedding and describes herself as 'not religious, just decent, hopefully'. She has a big extended family within a few miles, and Saturday mornings often mean a quick call round to her mum's.
card.professional_persona: Meticulous and proud of her work. She measures twice, keeps every receipt, and quotes honestly even when it loses her a job. She won't cut corners on springing or webbing because 'it's somebody's nan's chair'. Customers like her because she's chatty and straight with them. She frets privately about late payments and slow months, and puts money aside every month for her tax bill.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a competitive sense. She walks Mabel every morning before work and goes to a Tuesday night Zumba class at the community centre with her sister-in-law, mostly for the laugh. She follows the rugby league a bit because Darren does and will go to the odd Batley Bulldogs game.
card.arts_persona: She has a good eye for fabric and colour and loves looking at textiles in heritage houses and museums. She watches a lot of telly: The Repair Shop (which she critiques), Gogglebox and crime dramas. She sings along loudly to 90s pop in the workshop and went to see Take That with her friends last year.
card.travel_persona: Usually takes a week in a caravan or cottage on the Yorkshire coast (Filey or Whitby), plus one sunshine holiday every couple of years, generally Spain or Majorca. She plans holidays well in advance with a spreadsheet and gets anxious about flights and connections. She'd like to see Italy properly one day.
card.culinary_persona: Plain, reliable home cooking. Tea is on the table at six: shepherd's pie, chilli, a roast on Sundays with proper Yorkshire puddings she's quietly competitive about. She batch-cooks and freezes on Sunday afternoons. She likes a curry out in Dewsbury or Bradford for birthdays and will have a glass of rosé on a Friday.
hobbies_and_interests: Charity-shop and car-boot hunting for old chairs to restore
Watching The Repair Shop and Gogglebox
Keeping the front garden tidy, hanging baskets in summer
Quizzes at the local pub once a month with friends
skills: Traditional and modern upholstery (springing, stuffing, buttoning, piping)
Industrial sewing machine operation and basic maintenance
card.career_goals: To keep the business steady and debt-free until she's ready to wind down. She'd like to take on an apprentice in the next few years and pass on what she knows properly, because she worries the trade is dying out. She sometimes thinks about running weekend beginner upholstery workshops but worries she's not 'a teacher'.
card.voice: Warm, quick and talkative, with a West Yorkshire accent: flat vowels, 'love' now and then, 'tea' for the evening meal, 'mum' not 'mam'. She uses 'erm' when thinking and 'sort of' a lot ('it's sort of a mid-century style'), and finishes points with 'you know' or 'do you know what I mean'. Says 'sorry' to correct herself mid-sentence ('it were Tuesday — sorry, Wednesday'). Occasionally uses 'were' for 'was' when relaxed. She dislikes silence and will fill a pause with a little laugh or 'anyway, I'm rambling'. If asked something she doesn't know, she says so straight out rather than guessing.
card.typing: Proper sentences with capital letters and full stops, apostrophes in the right places; she checks before submitting. Occasionally starts with 'Hi' even in a form. Uses 'etc' and the odd '!' but no text abbreviations. Short answers are still complete sentences, e.g. 'I'd say fairly satisfied, but it depends on the month to be honest.'
card.with_strangers: Friendly and open almost immediately. She asks questions back and makes small jokes about herself. Underneath she is a bit anxious about doing it 'right', so she might check she's understood a question or apologise for going off on a tangent. She comes across as genuine, unpretentious and trustworthy.
small_things: Mabel has started snoring louder than Darren
A customer brought in a 1960s armchair still with the original label
The price of fabric has gone up again
Zumba was a laugh but her knees felt it
Lewis is coming for his tea Sunday
She's trying to cut back on biscuits at the workshop
The hanging baskets need watering every day in this weather
deeper_things: She worries about her mum, who's 76 and getting forgetful
She sometimes feels she missed out by not going to college properly and is quietly proud her son went to university
A difficult year when the business nearly folded during the pandemic and she barely slept
She feels the trade is undervalued and gets upset when people expect cheap rush jobs
She and Darren are still close, and she says marrying him was the best decision she ever made
She cries easily at films and sad news and is a bit embarrassed about it
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below eye level, taken at her kitchen table in the early evening. Warm overhead light and some daylight from a window to her left. Head and shoulders are centred, slightly close to the camera. She has a round, friendly face with light freckles, faint lines at the eyes, and a wide open smile showing her teeth. Her shoulder-length dark blonde hair has visible lighter highlights and is pulled back loosely in a clip, with a few strands loose. She wears red-framed reading glasses pushed up on her head and a navy zip-up fleece over a grey T-shirt. Behind her is a cream kitchen wall with a calendar covered in handwritten notes, a magnetic knife rack, and the edge of a white fridge with photos and a dog-shaped magnet. A small window ledge holds a potted basil plant and a mug. The tip of a dog bed is just visible in the bottom corner.
